route: scripted (procedural Blender geometry; no provider generation; face art reused from the P5-T6 UI atlas)

texturesSampled: ui/dice-d8 (shared UI atlas page, resident for the UI)
ui/dice-d8-glow (shared UI atlas glow page, the face emissive map)

lods: LOD0 only: a 40 mm die stays within the 1,500-triangle dice budget (DICE_LIMITS), so a LOD chain saves nothing measurable
bake: none: face art is the shared atlas page and brass is a factor (or the shared brass-polished set), so nothing is baked

frame.convention: src/dice/faces.ts die-local frame; identity orientation = DicePresenter's
frame.uv: TEXCOORD_0 is glTF (v down); loadDice flips v once so face UVs are in the UI atlas's bottom-left texture space

materialsUsed: factor-only polished brass named after the approved P4-T3 brass-polished set (bindable at runtime); the face slot samples the shared P5-T6 UI atlas page
license: Original work generated in Blender from a checked-in script; face art and style reference from Paul's paid Higgsfield plan (Terms of Use 4.4)

checks: face table (GLB extras and manifest) equals faces.ts and content/dice.ts
reimport gate (face-up UVs in the atlas cell, no mirrored UVs, Blender reimport)

approvals.notes: validate-generated-assets verdict is reported to the orchestrator, not self-recorded
original procedural geometry; face art from the P5-T6 atlas (its own provenance)
Paul approves the in-engine look (docs/blender-kit-project.md ruling 3)
blender-kit-pieces requires an independent >= 80/100 score; unscored means unaccepted

independentScore.scale: 0-100 visual fidelity to the art direction
independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the asset)

rubric.note: Up 2 from 26. Both v3 deductions are resolved. Flat strips: a vertical scan at x=560 now crosses the upper-left rail over y 311 to 334 as one continuous ramp from relL 0.10 to 0.63 instead of v3's two-step facet. The equator band at x=600 (y 373 to 396) carries two rolled specular peaks (0.70 and 0.78), so the rails read as rounded bevels. Lost outline: the shadow-side rail at y=460 (x 619 to 644) now measures relL 0.18 to 0.30 behind a 0.92 edge highlight, above the floor at 0.092, where v3 measured 0.05 to 0.07. The right die spans y 264 to 529 (266 px), and the rails are 23 to 25 px wide, 8.6 to 9.4% of die height, against 7.6% in v3. Points are lost because the brass is still only a rail frame around black panels. Panel 4's d20 reads as a solid brass body with inset faces, and here the faces read as cut-outs.

Up 3 from 19. The v3 numeral-value and glow deductions are resolved. The numeral core (top quartile of amber stroke pixels) measures #FEBF5A to #FDC05C on all four closeup numerals, relL 0.589 to 0.594, H37, S0.64 to 0.65 and V 0.99 to 1.00, against candle amber #F3BE65 (H37, S0.58, relL 0.57) and v3's #C08C53 (relL 0.30). The glow now bleeds into the face. Median relL by distance from the stroke is 0.16 to 0.20 at 1 px, 0.10 to 0.11 at 2 px, 0.063 to 0.079 at 4 px, 0.035 to 0.052 at 6 px and 0.02 to 0.03 at 8 px, against glass at 0.004 to 0.009, so the bleed runs about 6 to 8 px where v3 fell to the glass level within 2 px. The grazing left side face no longer goes blue-grey. Its glass is #2D281F (relL 0.022) and its numeral core #F3C074. Points are lost because the glyphs are a plain rounded sans laid flat on the panel, not panel 4's engraved numerals set into a brass-bevelled face, and no numeral light reaches the inner rail bevels.

Up 1 from 13. The v3 grazing-grey deduction is resolved: blue-grey pixels are 0.0% on both closeup dice and on all eight lineup dice, against up to 3.6% in v3. The rails now show a real specular roll. Hue-masked rail relL runs p10 0.191, p50 0.322, p90 0.572 and p99 0.668 on the right die, against 0.068, 0.159 and 0.197 (p10, p50, p90) in v3, so they read as metal more than the d6 frame does. Points are still lost on the faces and the wear. The panels are flat obsidian, relL 0.004 to 0.009 (#150B07 to #211611), with faint specks and no depth, refraction or warm interior, so a die named glass reads as black enamel. That is allowed by the bible's enamel option but is flatter than panel 4's faces (#3C2514, relL 0.023, with warm gradients). The rails have no edge wear, and their top 5% goes cream (#E6CE9B, S 0.33).

Up 2 from 11. The numerals are now on palette in hue, saturation and value (see signature). The blue-grey grazing face, which v3 called off-palette, is gone. The glass is near warm black (#150B07 to #211611, relL 0.004 to 0.009), slightly darker and redder than #231D1A (relL about 0.013), and it separates from the floor (#724F37, relL 0.094) at about 2.5:1 (v3 reported about 3:1 on similar glass values). The rails remain short of polished brass. The median is #AF975B (H43, S0.48, V0.69, relL 0.32) on the right die and #A89056 on the left, against #DEC16A (V 0.87, relL 0.55). That is lighter than v3's #876B30 (V 0.53) but still a pale champagne gold.

Up 1 from 9. v3 held a point back for the low numeral value and the grey grazing face, and both are resolved. Numeral-core-to-glass contrast measures 11.10:1 (left "1"), 11.89:1 (left "3"), 10.76:1 (right "7") and 11.65:1 (right "3"), against a v3 median of about 5.9:1. The grazing side-face numeral measures 8.78:1. All eight lineup dice measure 9.85 to 10.87:1 with numeral cores #EBB663 to #F7BC63 (S 0.58 to 0.61). The lineup dice are 65 to 94 px across, which is the size a 40 mm die subtends at about 0.7 m on Quest 3, and the face-up numeral is legible on each one. The evidence is still desktop only, and a headset capture should confirm it.

topFixes: Polish the brass rails toward #DEC16A. The median is #AF975B (V 0.69, relL 0.32) against relL 0.55, and the highlights go cream (#E6CE9B, S 0.33). Lift the base colour or the probe response, keep the specular tint gold, and add light edge wear at the vertices.

Give the face panels depth instead of a flat black cut-out. The glass is relL 0.004 to 0.009 everywhere outside the numeral glow. Add a warm interior gradient or subsurface pool around each numeral, near panel 4's face tone #3C2514 (relL about 0.023), so the panel reads as smoked glass or enamel. Let the numeral light catch the inner rail bevels.

Seat the numerals into the face. The glyphs are a plain rounded sans printed flat on the panel. An engraved or inset treatment with a thin brass or dark lip, like panel 4's d20, would tie them to the body.

Widen the brass bevel so each face sits inset in a brass body, as on panel 4's d20, instead of black panels framed by 23 to 25 px rails (8.6 to 9.4% of die height). Confirm the result in a Quest 3 headset capture at the seated table distance.
independentScore.method: Independent reviewer (did not build the asset). I read the palette and dice sections of docs/art-bible.md and the references listed in assets-source/dice/<die>/provenance.json (L-board-1.png, panel 4, cropped at (60,956)-(750,1490), same crop as v3). I did not open any author self-score, status file, build note or commit message. Primary evidence was the shipped in-engine stills in the worktree, identified by md5 and mtime 2026-11-16 20:01 PST because git was off-limits: docs/verification/p5-dice-brass-d6.jpg (ad88fc95), p5-dice-brass-d6-lineup.jpg (7b7b80db), p5-dice-glass-d8.jpg (ad77e919) and p5-dice-glass-d8-lineup.jpg (fa4b9984), all 960x640, cropped and upscaled 2x to 4x for inspection. The renderer and GPU were not verified by me. The Blender renders and assets-source/dice/dice.review-sheet.jpg were used for shape only, because they render every surface through AgX. Measurements used Pillow and NumPy under python3 -I (scripts in /tmp/rxr-prev/dv4/tools): median sRGB in fixed boxes, hue-masked brass (H38 to 60 or 62, S above 0.3, cross-checked at S above 0.45), pixel scans across rails, frames and well walls, and ring or dilation-distance profiles around pips and numerals. Contrast ratios are WCAG (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) on relative luminance. Palette targets in relL: polished brass #DEC16A 0.55, candle amber #F3BE65 0.57, warm black #231D1A about 0.013. Play distance: a 40 mm die at about 0.7 m subtends about 3.3 degrees, roughly 80 px at Quest 3's roughly 25 px per degree. All evidence is desktop only, with no headset capture. Date 2026-11-16. For d8: numeral cores are the top quartile of amber stroke pixels (H15 to 38, S above 0.45, relL above 0.15), glass is relL below 0.06 in each face box (below 0.03 in the lineup), and glow bleed is the median relL in successive 1 px dilation rings around the relL above 0.30 stroke, with brass excluded. Rail width and profile come from vertical and horizontal pixel scans across the right die.
